text: Ivan Dmitritch was an ordinary middle class man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who lived with his family. <break time="0.8s" /> On twelve hundred roubles a year. <break time="0.8s" /> And he was quite satisfied with his life. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening after supper. <break time="0.8s" /> He was sitting comfortably on the sofa. <break time="0.8s" /> And reading the newspaper in peace. <break time="0.8s" /> I forgot to look at the newspaper today. <break time="0.8s" /> Said his wife, Masha. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was clearing the table after the meal. <break time="0.8s" /> Will you look and see. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether the list of winning lottery numbers. <break time="0.8s" /> Is printed there. <break time="0.8s" /> She asked him. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes, it is here. <break time="0.8s" /> Ivan answered. <break time="0.8s" /> But is your ticket still good. <break time="0.8s" /> Or has it already run out. <break time="0.8s" /> It is still good. <break time="0.8s" /> Because I collected the interest on it. <break time="0.8s" /> On Tuesday. <break time="0.8s" /> Masha replied calmly. <break time="0.8s" /> What is the number. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked. <break time="0.8s" /> And she answered at once. <break time="0.8s" /> Series 9, 499, number 26. <break time="0.8s" /> Ivan did not believe in lottery luck. <break time="0.8s" /> And on any other evening. <break time="0.8s" /> He would not have bothered. <break time="0.8s" /> To look at the list at all. <break time="0.8s" /> But now he had nothing else to do so he lazily ran his finger. <break time="0.8s" /> Down the long column of numbers. <break time="0.8s" /> At once. <break time="0.8s" /> As if to laugh at his doubts. <break time="0.8s" /> The number 9, 499 jumped out at him. <break time="0.8s" /> From the second line from the top.
